raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`NixlEplbCommunicator` created its own NIXL agent and registered the expert weights with it. A
reconfiguration builds the replacement communicator while the old one is still alive, so a worker ended up
holding several agents with the same expert pages registered. On MI355 the extra IPC export is refused and
the test fails. This hands the replacement communicator the agent it is replacing, so the pages are
registered once, and adds the Elastic EP Scaling step on MI355.

## Claims

- A worker holds one NIXL agent over its expert weights instead of one per communicator ever built.
- `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py` passes on MI355, which it did not before.
- Nothing here is platform specific and nothing is gated on a platform. The extra registration happens on
  every backend; it is only fatal on some.

## Validation

**Agent count per worker process**, counted from `Initialized NIXL agent` lines in CI logs of
`tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py`, which runs four scale cycles:

| | processes | agents | processes holding more than one |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MI355X, unmodified, build 92231 | 12 | 18 | 5, one of them three |
| MI300X, unmodified | 16 | 31 | 8 |
| MI355X, with this change | 16 | 16 | 0 |
| H100, with this change | 20 | 20 | 0 |

Build 92231 ran this step on #56679, which adds Buildkite yaml and nothing else, so that is unmodified code. There MI355 reports `hipIpcGetMemHandle failed : invalid argument` 6 and 8 times and the test fails, while H100 passes in the same builds. The counts are lower than 16 because those runs failed part way through, so fewer workers reached the point of creating an agent.

The MI300X row is an unmodified run on hardware that tolerates the extra registrations. It shows the extra
registration is not specific to the platform where it breaks.

**The test.** The MI355 step failed on every attempt before this change. With it, the two most recent runs
were 4 passed, 1 skipped, in 857 s and 853 s, with zero `hipIpc* failed`, and the H100 step green in the same
builds. The fifth case skips on ROCm because NIXL EP is not installed in that image. Accuracy stays in the
H100 band: the largest deviation from the pre-scaling GSM8K score was 0.036 on MI355 and 0.035 on H100,
against a tolerance of 0.080.

## Details

**Root cause.** A NIXL registration belongs to the agent that made it, and `num_local_experts` is fixed, so
the expert weights and the receive buffers keep their storage across a reconfiguration. Building a fresh
agent for the replacement communicator therefore exports IPC handles for memory that is already exported,
and leaves the worker holding two and then three agents over the same pages.

**The fix.** `EplbState.create_communicator` already holds the communicator being replaced, so it passes it
down and the NIXL backend reuses its agent, registering memory only when it creates a fresh one. The agent
is dropped when the last communicator referencing it is collected, and NIXL deregisters the memory and
disconnects the peers from its destructor. `add_remote_agent` for a peer the shared agent already knows is a
no op, since `loadRemoteMD` merges into the existing entry and the connection info is unchanged.

This is @NickLucche's implementation, from a branch he wrote against this one. My first version kept a module
level registry keyed by the expert address range, which was more machinery for the same result.

**The `__del__` guard.** Separate and small, in the same teardown path. `__del__` can run during interpreter
shutdown, when module globals are already being set to `None`, including the `contextlib` that the teardown
body itself uses. The cleanup then raises and every worker prints a traceback on exit. The body is now
wrapped in a plain `try` that depends on no module.

**On the ROCm side.** A probe in the worker showed that at the moment a 6 MiB export is refused a 2 MiB one
from the same process still succeeds, and that shortly before the refusal the same process had completed 64
consecutive 6 MiB exports. So the refusal is narrower than the duplicate export alone would suggest, and
that part is being looked at separately in ROCm/rocm-systems#11892. This PR does not depend on that issue and
does not work around it: it removes the duplicate registration, which was worth removing on the vLLM side
regardless of how any runtime responds to it.

**CI steps.** The upstream step is the `mirror.amd` override of the existing H100 nightly step, so it
inherits `optional: true` and runs nightly on `mi355_4`. It overrides `commands` because ROCm installs the
KV connector requirements differently, and adds a pytest thread timeout so a hung scale cycle prints a
Python stack instead of being killed by the agent with an empty log. A matching MI355 step is added next to
the existing MI300 one in the AMD pipeline.


<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Two things I haven't seen raised yet:

**1. The CI part conflicts with #63609, and half of it merges silently.**

#63609 (merged 10-25) commented out both `:nvidia: (H100) [Nightly] Elastic EP Scaling` and `:amd: (MI300) Elastic EP Scaling` ("Disabled until the KV connectors installation is locked") and allowlisted `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py`. Against current main:

- `expert_parallelism.yaml` conflicts, because the parent of the `mirror: amd:` block no longer exists.
- `test-amd.yaml` auto-merges and leaves a live MI355 step right below the commented-out MI300 one. That step runs `uv pip install --system -r requirements/kv_connectors_rocm.txt` (unpinned `tblib`, `lm_eval[api]`), the same install #63609 commented out everywhere else in that file.

The install isn't needed on ROCm anyway. The ci_base image already installs the pinned `requirements/test/rocm.txt` (`tblib==3.1.0`, `lm-eval==0.4.12`) and the NIXL wheel, and the test only uses `evaluate_gsm8k`, which doesn't import lm_eval. I'd suggest a standalone top-level `device: mi355_4` step without the install line, like the MI355 steps in `e2e_integration.yaml`, and dropping the allowlist entry.

Minor: the rationale in the `--timeout=1800 --timeout-method=thread` comment doesn't hold.
- `run-amd-test.sh` already sets `PYTEST_TIMEOUT=2400`, `--timeout-method=thread` and `faulthandler_timeout=1500`.
- The scale cycle runs in the `vllm serve` subprocess, so a pytest-side stack dump wouldn't show it.
- A hung scale fails earlier, at `requests.post(..., timeout=300)`.

**2. The MI355 results predate #62827, which changes the transport (relevant to @itayalroy's scale-down point).**

Build 96848 ran on an image with the old UCX pin (`96e58a16`, `UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y`). Per #62827, NIXL never selected `rocm_ipc` at that pin, so the EPLB READs went through TCP emulation or the host-staged pipeline. After the rebase they go through `rocm_ipc`, so the pass/timing/accuracy results need a rerun on a main-based image. The registration-side export (`hsa_amd_ipc_memory_create` in mem_reg) is the same at both pins.

This also affects the scale-down disconnect. At the new pin (`2ff0b47c`), `rocm_ipc_cache.c` keeps imported handles in a process-global cache keyed by `(pid, pid_ns, dev_num)` (`UCX_ROCM_IPC_CACHE_IPC_HANDLES=y` by default). It only detaches a mapping on a conflicting import at the same address or in `UCS_STATIC_CLEANUP`, not on endpoint teardown. If I'm reading that right, `remove_remote_agent` on the surviving ranks won't release the removed ranks' HBM on ROCm; the pre-PR one-agent-per-communicator code wouldn't have either. It would be worth checking whether that HBM is actually freed after a 4→2 scale-down on MI355 with the new image.

> Adding remote agents concurrently with submitting xfers may be unsafe with `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_NONE`, and other modes might affect performance (not necessarily, just saying that it is something we need to investigate)

You're right, and the window is specific to this PR. The agent runs with NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_NONE (no listener thread, so that's the default), and add_remote_agent is called from _prepare_eplb_communicator during preparation, while the server is still serving and EPLB is only drained later at commit. Before this change each communicator built its own agent, so peers were added to an agent with nothing in flight; now a replacement communicator adds them to an agent the outgoing one may still be using.

On the cost of the stricter modes, I couldn't measure one. Under sustained load with step_interval=10, so 164 and 166 EPLB rearranges in two minutes, NONE gave 8.39 req/s at p50 2.207 s and STRICT gave 8.63 req/s at p50 2.144 s, with STRICT coming out marginally ahead, which puts the difference inside run-to-run noise.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I don't think NIXL behaves like this. Each agent has its own UCX context, and deregistering only drops that agent's own memh; another agent's registration over the same pages is unaffected. On ROCm, `rocm_ipc` dereg is just `ucs_free(key)`. The more likely issue is that every registration calls `hsa_amd_ipc_memory_create` on the base allocation again, which gfx950 rejects. Could you reword this, and share the UCX/HSA logs from the failing run if you have them?

On scale-down, we must disconnect from the NIXL agents of the removed ranks. Otherwise, UCX can retain IPC mappings to memory of the removed ranks, keeping the corresponding HBM allocated even after their vLLM processes exit and preventing that memory from being reused for anything else.

I measured this on MI355 with an image built from current main, so on the post-#62827 UCX pin where NIXL actually selects rocm_ipc.

You're right that the memory is retained, and it's worse than a one-off. Each departing card keeps about 14 GiB, and running repeated cycles against one long-lived server it grows by exactly 13728 MiB every cycle: 14374, 28102, 41830 MiB. The dp=4 peak grows with it against a 294896 MiB card, so a server doing this fails around the fifth scale-up. Scale-down timing stays flat throughout, so nothing in the current test would catch it.

remove_remote_agent doesn't recover it. Single-cycle test with main's teardown and with this PR's version gave a byte-identical 14376 MiB, in all four params. The cause is the UCX import cache @abmfy pointed at, which isn't tied to the agent. Disabling it keeps the residue flat at 645 MiB across cycles, costing about 1.6 s per scale-down.

So there is a real leak and a fix that works, just not on the agent side. Do you want it in this PR or a follow-up?

does not work around it: it removes the duplicate registration, which was worth removing on the vLLM side
regardless of how any runtime responds to it.

**CI steps.** The upstream step is the `mirror.amd` override of the existing H100 nightly step, so it
inherits `optional: true` and runs nightly on `mi355_4`. It overrides `commands` because ROCm installs the
KV connector requirements differently, and adds a pytest thread timeout so a hung scale cycle prints a
Python stack instead of being killed by the agent with an empty log. A matching MI355 step is added next to
the existing MI300 one in the AMD pipeline.

inline_comments.body: I don't think NIXL behaves like this. Each agent has its own UCX context, and deregistering only drops that agent's own memh; another agent's registration over the same pages is unaffected. On ROCm, `rocm_ipc` dereg is just `ucs_free(key)`. The more likely issue is that every registration calls `hsa_amd_ipc_memory_create` on the base allocation again, which gfx950 rejects. Could you reword this, and share the UCX/HSA logs from the failing run if you have them?

On scale-down, we must disconnect from the NIXL agents of the removed ranks. Otherwise, UCX can retain IPC mappings to memory of the removed ranks, keeping the corresponding HBM allocated even after their vLLM processes exit and preventing that memory from being reused for anything else.

Note that removing remote agents for scale down cannot be done during EEP preparation, as EPLB still runs and we can accidentally remove an agent while reading/writing from/to its memory. This means we also need to understand the impact of this work on scale-down downtime

inline_comments.body:
I measured this on MI355 with an image built from current main, so on the post-#62827 UCX pin where NIXL actually selects rocm_ipc.

You're right that the memory is retained, and it's worse than a one-off. Each departing card keeps about 14 GiB, and running repeated cycles against one long-lived server it grows by exactly 13728 MiB every cycle: 14374, 28102, 41830 MiB. The dp=4 peak grows with it against a 294896 MiB card, so a server doing this fails around the fifth scale-up. Scale-down timing stays flat throughout, so nothing in the current test would catch it.

remove_remote_agent doesn't recover it. Single-cycle test with main's teardown and with this PR's version gave a byte-identical 14376 MiB, in all four params. The cause is the UCX import cache @abmfy pointed at, which isn't tied to the agent. Disabling it keeps the residue flat at 645 MiB across cycles, costing about 1.6 s per scale-down.

So there is a real leak and a fix that works, just not on the agent side. Do you want it in this PR or a follow-up?

Both steps pass with your branch merged in. MI355 is 4 passed, 1 skipped, H100 is 5 passed, and Initialized NIXL agent now counts 16 across 16 processes on MI355 and 20 across 20 on H100, none holding more than one, with zero`hipIpc* failed` on either.

The only thing left in the H100 log is two AsyncLLM output_handler failed tracebacks at shutdown. That race is on main and not related to this change, I will cover that in a separate PR.
The `async_llm.py` change is now on the PR #63337.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @stefankoncarevic.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Two things I haven't seen raised yet:

**1. The CI part conflicts with #63609, and half of it merges silently.**

#63609 (merged 10-25) commented out both `:nvidia: (H100) [Nightly] Elastic EP Scaling` and `:amd: (MI300) Elastic EP Scaling` ("Disabled until the KV connectors installation is locked") and allowlisted `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py`. Against current main:

- `expert_parallelism.yaml` conflicts, because the parent of the `mirror: amd:` block no longer exists.
- `test-amd.yaml` auto-merges and leaves a live MI355 step right below the commented-out MI300 one. That step runs `uv pip install --system -r requirements/kv_connectors_rocm.txt` (unpinned `tblib`, `lm_eval[api]`), the same install #63609 commented out everywhere else in that file.

The install isn't needed on ROCm anyway. The ci_base image already installs the pinned `requirements/test/rocm.txt` (`tblib==3.1.0`, `lm-eval==0.4.12`) and the NIXL wheel, and the test only uses `evaluate_gsm8k`, which doesn't import lm_eval. I'd suggest a standalone top-level `device: mi355_4` step without the install line, like the MI355 steps in `e2e_integration.yaml`, and dropping the allowlist entry.

Minor: the rationale in the `--timeout=1800 --timeout-method=thread` comment doesn't hold.
- `run-amd-test.sh` already sets `PYTEST_TIMEOUT=2400`, `--timeout-method=thread` and `faulthandler_timeout=1500`.
- The scale cycle runs in the `vllm serve` subprocess, so a pytest-side stack dump wouldn't show it.
- A hung scale fails earlier, at `requests.post(..., timeout=300)`.

**2. The MI355 results predate #62827, which changes the transport (relevant to @itayalroy's scale-down point).**

Build 96848 ran on an image with the old UCX pin (`96e58a16`, `UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y`). Per #62827, NIXL never selected `rocm_ipc` at that pin, so the EPLB READs went through TCP emulation or the host-staged pipeline. After the rebase they go through `rocm_ipc`, so the pass/timing/accuracy results need a rerun on a main-based image. The registration-side export (`hsa_amd_ipc_memory_create` in mem_reg) is the same at both pins.

This also affects the scale-down disconnect. At the new pin (`2ff0b47c`), `rocm_ipc_cache.c` keeps imported handles in a process-global cache keyed by `(pid, pid_ns, dev_num)` (`UCX_ROCM_IPC_CACHE_IPC_HANDLES=y` by default). It only detaches a mapping on a conflicting import at the same address or in `UCS_STATIC_CLEANUP`, not on endpoint teardown. If I'm reading that right, `remove_remote_agent` on the surviving ranks won't release the removed ranks' HBM on ROCm; the pre-PR one-agent-per-communicator code wouldn't have either. It would be worth checking whether that HBM is actually freed after a 4→2 scale-down on MI355 with the new image.

> Adding remote agents concurrently with submitting xfers may be unsafe with `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_NONE`, and other modes might affect performance (not necessarily, just saying that it is something we need to investigate)

You're right, and the window is specific to this PR. The agent runs with NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_NONE (no listener thread, so that's the default), and add_remote_agent is called from _prepare_eplb_communicator during preparation, while the server is still serving and EPLB is only drained later at commit. Before this change each communicator built its own agent, so peers were added to an agent with nothing in flight; now a replacement communicator adds them to an agent the outgoing one may still be using.

On the cost of the stricter modes, I couldn't measure one. Under sustained load with step_interval=10, so 164 and 166 EPLB rearranges in two minutes, NONE gave 8.39 req/s at p50 2.207 s and STRICT gave 8.63 req/s at p50 2.144 s, with STRICT coming out marginally ahead, which puts the difference inside run-to-run noise.

So I've switched the EPLB agent to NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_STRICT. It only applies to the agent I create, so nothing else using NIXL is affected. Full suite on MI355 with the change is 4 passed, 1 skipped in 762 s, with scale and downtime numbers unchanged.

> * A hung scale fails earlier, at `requests.post(..., timeout=300)`.
> 
> **2. The MI355 results predate #62827, which changes the transport (relevant to @itayalroy's scale-down point).**
> 
> Build 96848 ran on an image with the old UCX pin (`96e58a16`, `UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y`). Per #62827, NIXL never selected `rocm_ipc` at that pin, so the EPLB READs went through TCP emulation or the host-staged pipeline. After the rebase they go through `rocm_ipc`, so the pass/timing/accuracy results need a rerun on a main-based image. The registration-side export (`hsa_amd_ipc_memory_create` in mem_reg) is the same at both pins.
> 
> This also affects the scale-down disconnect. At the new pin (`2ff0b47c`), `rocm_ipc_cache.c` keeps imported handles in a process-global cache keyed by `(pid, pid_ns, dev_num)` (`UCX_ROCM_IPC_CACHE_IPC_HANDLES=y` by default). It only detaches a mapping on a conflicting import at the same address or in `UCS_STATIC_CLEANUP`, not on endpoint teardown. If I'm reading that right, `remove_remote_agent` on the surviving ranks won't release the removed ranks' HBM on ROCm; the pre-PR one-agent-per-communicator code wouldn't have either. It would be worth checking whether that HBM is actually freed after a 4→2 scale-down on MI355 with the new image.

All of this is in.

expert_parallelism.yaml now has a standalone device: mi355_4 step instead of the mirror block, and the uv pip install line and the --timeout flags are gone from it and from test-amd.yaml. The allowlist entry didn't need touching: #64010 already dropped it when it re-enabled the MI300 step.

Reran on rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-f7d949c58b19bd0a, which is on the new pin: 4 passed, 1 skipped in 762 s.

Your reading of rocm_ipc_cache.c is correct, remove_remote_agent included. Numbers are in @itayalroy's thread, and the residue turns out to accumulate per scale cycle.
